problems.title: Two congruences with a common target
problems.question: Find the greatest nonpositive integern with n≡9mod5 and n≡9mod6.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: Both conditions mean n−9 is divisible bylcm(5,6)=30.
steps: Thusn=9+30k. The greatest nonpositive choice is k=−1, givingn=−21.

problems.title: Which sequence has two-sided bounds?
problems.question: Amonga_n=n+1/n, b_n=(2n−1)/(n+1), c_n=−n²−4n+7, which is bounded above and below?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
steps: For positive integern,1/2≤b_n<2, so it is bounded both ways.
a_n grows without bound, andc_n tends to −∞. Thus onlyb_n qualifies.

problems.title: Convert all bases to powers of two
problems.question: Evaluate[4^(−0.25)+(2^1.5)^(−2/3)]·[4^(−0.25)−(2√2)^(−2/3)].
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: $4^{-1/4}=1/\sqrt2$, and both remaining powers equal2⁻¹=1/2.

problems.title: An annulus around a regular polygon
problems.question: A regularn-gon has sidea. Find the are a between its circumcircle and incircle.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: CircumradiusR, inradiusr, and half-sidea/2 for m a right triangle, so R²−r²=a²/4.
steps: The annulus are a is π(R²−r²)=πa²/4, independent ofn.

problems.title: Sector formulas in radians
problems.question: A sector has angle 1radian and arc length 2. Find are a.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: Arc lengthl=Rθ and are a S=R²θ/2.
steps: ThusR=2 and S=2²·1/2=2.

problems.title: Compare successive sequence terms
problems.question: Which sequences increase:a_n=n^(−1/3), b_n=n/(n+3), c_n=n²−20n+9?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
steps: Asn increases, the subtracted fraction decreases, so b_n increases.
a_n decreases; c_n initially decreases and later increases because its vertex is at n=10. Thus onlyb_n is increasing for all positive integer indices.

problems.title: Choose the nearest integer to the vertex
problems.question: Find the index of the greatest term ofa_n=−n²+√75·n−9.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: The real vertex is at n=√75/2≈4.330.
steps: The nearest positive integer is 4. A concave quadratic falls as the distance from its vertex increases, so the greatest sequence term is the fourth.

problems.title: Extremes on either side of a missing index
problems.question: Find maximum plus minimum ofa_n=(4n+1)/(n−5).
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: $a_n=4+21/(n-5)$, with n=5 excluded.
steps: For1≤n≤4, the smallest value occurs at 4 and is −17. Forn≥6, the largest occurs at 6 and is 25.
Their sum is 8.
problems.note: The displayed formula is undefined at n=5. The answer uses all its defined positive-integer terms.

problems.title: Circle inside a minor circular segment
problems.question: A120° minor segment contains a circle tangent to its chord at the midpoint and internally tangent to the original circle. Find the large/small are a ratio.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: The chord is distance Rcos60°=R/2 from the large centre. The segment height is R−R/2=R/2.
steps: The small circle’s diameter equals this segment height, so its radius is R/4.
The are a ratio is R²/(R/4)²=16:1.

problems.title: Area of an asymmetric circular lens
problems.question: Two circles have radii1,√3 and centre distance 2. Find their intersection are a.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: The triangle of the two centres and an intersection point is right, with centre angles60° and 30°.
steps: The two lens sectors therefore have angles120°,60° andareasπ/3,π/2.
The two triangles removed from these sectors together have are a √3.
The lens are a is π/3+π/2−√3=(5π−6√3)/6.

problems.title: Compare exponents in an identity
problems.question: For everyx>0, fifth-root(x⁸·cube-rootx)=(x^(−0.6k²))^(1/k). Findk.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: The left exponent is(8+1/3)/5=5/3. For k≠0, the right exponent is −(3/5)k.
steps: Equality for every positive base requires5/3=−3k/5. Thusk=−25/9.
problems.answer: k=−25/9; none of the listed choices.
problems.note: The fifth-root index and eighth power in the source give−25/9, which is absent from the options.

problems.title: One open solution interval inside another
problems.question: For whicha is the solution set ofx²−x−2<0 contained in that ofx²+4x−a<0?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: The first interval is(−1,2). Requirea>x²+4x throughout that open interval.
steps: The supremum ofx²+4x there is 12, approached at the excluded endpoint2.
Thus a=12 works, and everya>12 works. Ifa<12, inputs sufficiently close to 2 fail.

problems.title: Factor in cube-root variables
problems.question: Simplify[(x^(4/3)−2x^(2/3)y^(2/3)+y^(4/3))/(x−x^(2/3)y^(1/3)−x^(1/3)y^(2/3)+y)]/(x^(1/3)+y^(1/3)).
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: Put u=∛x, v=∛y. The numerator is(u−v)²(u+v)²; the first denominator is(u−v)²(u+v).
steps: The extra denominator supplies a second factoru+v. Everything cancels to 1 wherever the original denominators are nonzero.

problems.title: Equal polygon areas compare circumradii
problems.question: A regular hexagon and octagon have equal are a. Find the ratio of their circumcircle areas, hexagon first.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: Hexagonarea=(3√3/2)R₆²; octagonarea=2√2R₈².
steps: Equating gives R₆²/R₈²=4√2/(3√3)=4√6/9. The circle-are a ratio is the same.

problems.title: Sum of distances to equal polygon sides
problems.question: Every-other-side midpoints of a regular dodecagon for m a regular hexagon of circumradius2. Find the sum of distances from an interior point to all 12 sides.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: Those midpoints lie on the dodecagon incircle, so its inradius is 2. Splitting the polygon into12 triangles gives side·(distance sum)/2=polygon are a.
steps: Since the polygon are a is 12·side·inradius/2, the distance sum is 12·2=24, independent of the chosen interior point.

problems.title: Solve two small congruences
problems.question: Find the digit sum of the least positive integerx satisfyingx+13≡3mod8 and x−3≡1mod6.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: These reduce tox≡6mod8 and x≡4mod6.
steps: Numbers6,14,22,… in the first class first meet the second at 22.
The digit sum is 2+2=4.

problems.title: A quadratic negative between its roots
problems.question: Which condition describes quadratics whose two roots satisfy(x₁−1)(x₂−1)<0?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: By Vieta,(x₁−1)(x₂−1)=(a+b+c)/a.
steps: Thus the equivalent condition is a(a+b+c)<0. It forces a≠0 and P(1) to have the opposite sign from the leading coefficient, which also guarantees two distinct real roots surrounding1.

problems.title: An alternating recurrence
problems.question: a₁=1, a_(n+1)=a_n+(−1)^n. Finda₁₉₉.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: The first terms are 1,0,1,0,… .
steps: Odd-indexed terms are 1, so a₁₉₉=1.

problems.title: Smallest circumcircle of a fixed-area right triangle
problems.question: A right triangle has are a 3. Find the least possible circumcircle are a.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: For legsu, v, uv=6 andhypotenuse²=u²+v²≥2uv=12. Circumradius is half the hypotenuse.
steps: ThusR²≥3 and circlearea≥3π. Equal legsu=v=√6 attain the bound.

problems.title: Equilateral area from circumcircle area
problems.question: An equilateral triangle’s circumcircle has are a 12π. Find triangle are a.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: R²=12, side²=3R²=36.
steps: Triangle are a=(√3/4)·36=9√3.

problems.title: Power cycles modulo seven
problems.question: Find the one-digit residuex for 2¹⁹⁹+11⁹ modulo7.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: Powers of 2 have period3 modulo7;199≡1mod3. Also11≡4 and 4³≡1mod7.
steps: Thus2¹⁹⁹≡2,11⁹≡1, and their sum is 3.

problems.title: One universal identity and two counterexamples
problems.question: Which claims hold for every positiven:I n²+n+43 is prime; II the firstn+1 odd numbers sum to(n+1)²; III5^[n(n+1)/2]+2^[n(n+1)/2] is divisible by 7?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: The sum of the firstk odd numbers isk².
steps: II is true with k=n+1. I fails at n=1, where the value is 45.
III fails at n=3:the exponent is 6, and modulo7 both 5⁶ and 2⁶ equal1, so their sum is 2.

problems.title: Exactly nine integers in a quadratic interval
problems.question: For whicha doesax²+10ax−a−5>0 have exactly 9 integer solutions?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: Ifa≥0, the set has either infinitely many integer solutions(a>0) ornone(a=0). For a<0, it becomes(x+5)²<26+5/a.
steps: An interval centred at integer −5 contains exactly 9 integers precisely when offsets−4,…,4 are included but±5 are not.
Thus16<26+5/a≤25. Solving with a<0 gives −5≤a<−1/2.

problems.title: Sector perimeter and area together
problems.question: A sector has perimeter28 andarea49. Find its arc lengthl.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
steps: Substitute l=28−2R into Rl=98 to obtain R²−14R+49=0.
ThusR=7 and l=28−14=14.

problems.title: A contact chord’s minor segment
problems.question: A circle touches AB, AC of an equilateral side-5 triangle at M, N, and intersects BC. IfMB=2, find the minor segment are a cut by MN.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant exact identity and check boundaries or exceptional inputs.
formulas: AM=5−2=3. In the 60° wedge, the radius is r=AMtan30°=√3, and the central contact angle MON=120°.
steps: The sector are a is(120/360)πr²=π. The triangle MON are a is(1/2)r²sin120°=3√3/4.
Their difference is π−3√3/4.
